entries.title: Show writing systems
entries.description: Reads fonts, features, direction and style sizes from the current Baseline, in FieldWorks writing-system order. Change these settings in FieldWorks, then capture a new Baseline to read them here.
entries.helpPage:
# Show writing systems

`motif writing-systems --project <fwdata> [--json]` reads the current [Baseline](term:baseline)'s writing systems without opening the FieldWorks project. Before the first capture, it reports that no Baseline exists.

Each current vernacular and analysis list keeps FieldWorks' order and default. The response includes the id, name, abbreviation, requested default font family, verbatim feature string, direction, and each style's effective font, features and point size. A writing system in both lists appears once per membership; positions in JSON count from zero.

The command includes every project style; a missing style uses that writing system's effective Normal settings. Normal without a size uses FieldWorks' 10-point default. Sizes contain no window units or zoom.

For which FieldWorks style each part of the window uses and where to change its writing-system settings, see [Writing systems in the window](guide:writing-systems).

The font name is the project's request. The command reports saved settings and does not inspect installed fonts.

entries.title: Proposals
entries.description: Proposals lists every set of changes you can review: the Proposals an AI assistant put together, and the changes you collected yourself that are not applied yet. Each card shows what it changes and four numbers, today's beside what they would be with the Proposal.
entries.helpPage:
# Proposals

**Proposals** lists every set of changes you can review: the Proposals an AI assistant put together, and the changes you collected yourself that are not applied yet. Each card shows what it changes and four numbers, today's beside what they would be with the Proposal.

The cards are grouped by what to do next:

- **Waiting for you** has been tried against the project as it is now and is ready to read.
- **Needs another try** was tried, but the project or the Proposal changed since, or the try did not finish. Its numbers are from that try, and nothing re-runs until you ask.
- **Not tried yet** has no Trial. Choose **Try it** to measure it.
- **Your changes not applied yet** are the changes you collected on **Texts**; they are also listed on **Review changes**.
- **Closed** lists the Proposals that were applied, declined, superseded or withdrawn. They are hidden until you choose **Show closed**, and **Hide closed** hides them again.

A card names what the Proposal changes in one line, such as “2 rules · 1 allomorph · 1 parse approved”. Its four numbers are Text Coverage, approved words kept, word time and warnings. A number that moved is shown in bold. A chip can say that approved words were lost, that a change no longer fits, or that another Proposal also changes some of the same words. A Proposal that only approves or removes analyses measures only the words it touches; every other word keeps today's value, so its totals still compare with today's.

Choose **Open** to see the project's pages with the Proposal beside today: the numbers on **Overview**, **Texts**, **Timing** and **Warnings** show today's value and the Proposal's. Choose **Try again** on a card that needs another try to measure it on a copy of the project. The copy is thrown away; your FieldWorks project is not changed.

Each card beside its name says where the Proposal is: **Draft**, **Ready**, **Deferred**, **Applied**, **Declined**, **Superseded** or **Withdrawn**. Your own changes carry no such word. A declined, superseded or withdrawn card offers **Delete**, which removes the Proposal and its tries. An applied Proposal cannot be deleted; it and its record of what was applied are kept.

The number beside **Proposals** in the sidebar counts the cards that are waiting for you.

entries.title: Review a Proposal
entries.description: When a Proposal is open, Review changes names it in the heading, such as “Sound change · 4 changes”, and lists every change in it in one order: the Grammar changes first, a change that others depend on before the ones that depend on it, then changes to words, grouped as they are for your own changes. You can read that list without applying anything.
entries.helpPage:
# Review a Proposal

When a Proposal is open, **Review changes** names it in the heading, such as “Sound change · 4 changes”, and lists every change in it in one order: the **Grammar changes** first, a change that others depend on before the ones that depend on it, then changes to words, grouped as they are for your own changes. You can read that list without applying anything.

1. Choose **Next** to move down the list. Choosing **Next** marks the change you leave as looked at; **Previous** moves back and marks nothing. **Keep** marks the current change and moves on, and **Keep all**, which shows how many it marks, marks every change. Every change, grammar or word, has its own **Keep** and **Undo** at the end of its row, and shows **✓ Looked at** once it has been looked at.
2. Read the count beside the buttons, such as “2 of 4 looked at”. Looking at a change is attention, not approval. Apply never waits for it, and it never changes the Proposal.
3. Choose **Undo** beside a change you do not want. If other changes depend on it, Motif names them first, such as “Undoing “Voicing rule before vowels” also undoes “Retarget the restriction to the new rule”.” Choose **Undo both** (or **Undo these 3** when there are more), or **Cancel** to leave everything as it was.
4. After an Undo, the Proposal needs another try, because what it was tried against has changed. Choose **Try again**. Nothing re-runs on its own.
5. Choose **Apply to FieldWorks project** when Apply is no longer blocked. The Apply card lists what Apply checks, each with ✓ or ✗: whether the Proposal was tried as it is now, whether every change still fits, and whether it is ready to apply.

Choose **Decline** if you do not want the Proposal at all. It is kept with its tries as a record, the window leaves it, and its card moves to **Closed** on **Proposals**, where **Reopen** opens it again.

A change stops counting as looked at when the change itself changes, or when the Proposal is tried again. An undone change leaves the count. Keyboard shortcuts for this list are in [Keyboard shortcuts](guide:keyboard-shortcuts).
